question: A dishonest dealer sells articles at 15% loss on cost price but uses the weight of 20 g instead of 25 g. What is his profit or loss percentage?
solution:
**Given:**

A dishonest dealer sells articles at 15% loss on cost price.

**Concept:**

Loss = Cost price - Selling price

**Formula used:**

P\%={SP-CPover CP}× 100 Where, P = Profit, SP = Selling price, and CP = Cost price

**Calculation:**

Let the cost price of the 25 g article be X.

The selling price of the article = {(1 - {15over 100})} × X={({100-15over100})} × X={85over100} × X=0.85X

The cost price of the 20g article = {Xover 25} × 20={4Xover5}

The profit percentage = {0.85X-0.8Xover0.8X}× 100={0.05Xover 0.8X}× 100={0.0625 × 100}=6.25\%

**∴ The required result will be 6.25% Profit.**

-----------------------------

16 : 17

SP > CP so it is profit

Profit% = (1/16) × 100 = 6.25% profit.

∴ The required result will be 6.25% Profit.
